I read the whole file. It contains one theorem, `solution`, preceded by a long block of `attribute [-instance]` and `attribute [-simp]` lines. The file declares no simp lemmas, defines no simp-normal forms and adds no `@[simp]` attributes. The proof uses no `simp`, `simp_all`, `simpa` or `simp only`. It runs on `obtain`, `haveI`, `rw`, `exact`, and `RingHom.ext fun _ => rfl`. So I found no missing canonical simp lemma, no wrongly oriented rewrite, no competing rules and no cycle here.

The `attribute [-simp]` block locally disables many simp lemmas from other files. These are structure `injEq` and `sizeOf_spec` lemmas and some `*_apply` and `*_obj` lemmas. This looks like a harness-level setup that keeps those declarations out of the proof environment. Since the proof never calls simp, the removals change nothing in this file. I did not open the source files that define those lemmas. I therefore have no evidence about whether their simp attributes are badly designed in their own files, and I did not report them. The rubric needs a specific expression and a specific rule change that I can check, and I have neither.
